target.title: fix(media-core): detect MIME from encoded URL extensions
target.body:
Fixes encoded HTTP(S) media URLs such as `render%2Emp4` being treated as unknown by the media-core MIME fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users or plugins that pass media URLs with percent-encoded filename extensions could get an unknown MIME result when the URL still points to a supported file type.

For example, a normal URL such as:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4?download=1
```

is classified as `video/mp4`, but the encoded filename equivalent:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1
```

misses the `.mp4` extension on current `main` because the URL pathname remains percent-encoded before `path.extname()` runs. That affects the shared `mimeTypeFromFilePath()` / `detectMime({ filePath })` fallback used by media callers when no stronger MIME signal is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior scoped to HTTP(S) URL filename extension lookup in `getFileExtension()`. It extracts the final URL pathname segment first, decodes only that filename segment before extracting the extension, and falls back to the original filename segment if that segment contains malformed percent encoding.

This does not add a shared filename decoder, does not parse `Content-Disposition`, does not change local path fallback behavior, and does not let encoded path separators after an extension turn a non-filename suffix into a media extension. It only makes encoded URL filenames follow the same MIME classification path as the equivalent decoded filename.

## User Impact

Media URLs whose filename encodes the extension dot can now be classified like their ordinary URL equivalents.

Examples that now flow through the expected media MIME fallback:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1 -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Em%70%34         -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2EMP4            -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm             -> video/webm
```

That helps downstream media handling choose the correct behavior when a CDN or provider returns encoded URL filename components.

## Evidence

Behavior proof from current `main` before this change:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4?download=1   -> video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1 -> undefined
https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm             -> undefined
```

After-fix terminal proof from the PR branch using the actual media-core helpers:

```text
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4?download=1 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2Em%70%34 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render%2EMP4 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/webm; detectMime=video/webm
https://cdn.example.com/bad%ZZ/render%2Emp4 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/archive%2Fclip.mp4 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/archive%2Fclip%2Emp4 -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=video/mp4; detectMime=video/mp4
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4%2Fpreview -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=undefined; detectMime=undefined
https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4%5Cpreview -> mimeTypeFromFilePath=undefined; detectMime=undefined
```

Focused coverage now exercises the shared media-core fallback and the edge cases called out by the URL filename-decoding review:

```text
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render%2Em%70%34") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render%2EMP4") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/clip%2Ewebm") === "video/webm"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/bad%ZZ/render%2Emp4") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/archive%2Fclip%2Emp4") === "video/mp4"
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4%2Fpreview") === undefined
mimeTypeFromFilePath("https://cdn.example.com/render.mp4%5Cpreview") === undefined
detectMime({ filePath: "https://cdn.example.com/render%2Emp4?download=1" }) === "video/mp4"
```

Validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       111 passed (111)

git diff --check
passed
```

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. Purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — focused regression test exercises the changed expressions via `forceAccountBinding` gate:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

New test "renders account count via forceAccountBinding gate (exercises accounts.length, not dead || 1)":
- Configures a channel plugin with `forceAccountBinding: true`, 1 enabled+configured account
- Calls the real `buildChannelsTable()` — the production function from this branch
- Asserts `expect(row?.detail).toContain("accounts 1")` — proving the changed expressions ARE reached
- Output is `"accounts 1"` with or without `|| 1` — the fix changes nothing for the output

```
$ npx oxlint src/commands/status-all/channels.ts src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts
→ exit 0
```

**What was not tested:** `openclaw status --all` CLI end-to-end. The vitest test exercises the same `buildChannelsTable` function with forceAccountBinding, reaching the same three changed expressions the CLI would hit.

## Regression Test Plan

- `$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 10 tests passed** (9 existing + 1 new forceAccountBinding test)
- `$ npx oxlint src/commands/status-all/channels.ts src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts` — **0 errors**
- `$ git diff --stat` — **2 files, +28/-3**

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`: the `!anyEnabled` guard (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before reaching lines 382-403, and the `configuredAccounts.length > 0` guard (line 418) guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0` via the subset relation (line 285). The `|| 1` was a defensive pattern added without tracing the full control flow.

target.title: fix(block-reply): flush buffered text in coalescer stop() to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
## Summary 📌

The block-reply coalescer's `stop()` silently dropped buffered sub-minChars text instead of delivering it, causing Telegram DM replies to lose their final tail. `stop()` now synchronously delivers any buffered text before clearing the timer.

- Problem: `coalescer.stop()` only called `clearIdleTimer()`, discarding any buffered text that hadn't reached `minChars`. Agent-runner line 2630 calls `stop()` without a prior `flush({force:true})`, so the final text tail in a long reply was silently dropped with no error or log.
- Solution: Make `stop()` synchronously construct and deliver the buffered payload (fire-and-forget via `void onFlush(...)`) before clearing the buffer, guarded by `shouldAbort()` to avoid delivering during an active abort.
- What changed: `src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.ts` (new `deliverBufferedBeforeStop` helper preserving all 7 buffered visibility flags including `isCommentary`, `stop` now points to it), `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` (4 regression tests), `src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` (2 pipeline-level stop-delivery tests)
- What did NOT change: `flush()` logic, `enqueue()` logic, `shouldAbort()` behavior inside `flush()`, pipeline-level `flush`/`stop` ordering, `BlockStreamingCoalesceSchema` config surface, `flushOnEnqueue` exposure (tracked separately in #102580). All 7 buffered visibility flags (`isReasoning`, `isCommentary`, `isCompactionNotice`, `isFallbackNotice`, `isStatusNotice`, `replyToId`, `audioAsVoice`) are preserved in the stop() payload, matching `flush()` parity.

## Change Type (select all) 📌

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all) 📌

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR 📌

- Related to #102578
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation 📌

With block streaming enabled, the tail of a long assistant reply in a Telegram DM was silently dropped (never sent, no error logged). The coalescer supports `stop()` callers that don't force-flush first (agent-runner line 2630 in recovery/error paths), but `stop()` only cleared the idle timer without delivering buffered text.

The reporter confirmed 2 occurrences on 2026-07-09 with OpenClaw 2026.6.11, and both the issue reporter and ClawSweeper traced the root cause to the coalescer's `stop()` implementation.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) 📌

- Behavior addressed: `coalescer.stop()` silently drops buffered sub-minChars text instead of delivering it
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x64), Node 22.19, branch `fix/block-coalescer-stop-flush-102578`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  81 passed (81)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  28 passed (28)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  68 passed (68)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/ --run
Test Files  9 passed (9)
     Tests  176 passed (176)
```

New regression tests (6 tests across 2 files):

| Test case | File | Input | Expected |
|-----------|------|-------|----------|
| `stop() delivers buffered sub-minChars text` | reply-utils | enqueue 26-char text, minChars=800, stop() | text delivered |
| `stop() does not deliver when shouldAbort()=true` | reply-utils | enqueue text, set aborted=true, stop() | nothing delivered |
| `stop() after force-flush is idempotent` | reply-utils | enqueue 2 texts, flush({force:true}), stop() | exactly 1 delivery |
| `stop() preserves isCommentary` | reply-utils | enqueue commentary text, stop() | isCommentary=true preserved |
| `stop() delivers sub-minChars at pipeline level` | block-reply-pipeline | enqueue text below minChars, pipeline.stop() | text delivered via onBlockReply |
| `stop() flushes multiple coalesced chunks` | block-reply-pipeline | enqueue 3 small chunks, pipeline.stop() | all 3 coalesced and delivered |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `stop()` now delivers buffered text that was previously silently dropped
  2. `stop()` correctly skips delivery when `shouldAbort()` returns true
  3. `stop()` after a prior `flush({force:true})` is idempotent — no double delivery
  4. `stop()` preserves `isCommentary` so commentary suppression gates still apply
  5. Pipeline-level `stop()` without prior force-flush delivers buffered text through `onBlockReply`
  6. All 176 existing + new tests continue to pass across 3 test suites

- What was not tested: Real Telegram DM block-streaming end-to-end with a gateway instance (requires Crabbox + Telegram bot setup)

## Root Cause

`createBlockReplyCoalescer.stop()` was defined as `() => clearIdleTimer()`. It cleared the idle timer but did not deliver any buffered text. The main agent runner has two stop paths:

| Call site | Code | Safe? |
|-----------|------|-------|
| agent-runner:1803-1805 | `await flush({force:true}); stop()` | ✅ force-flush first |
| agent-runner:2630 | `stop()` only | ❌ buffered text dropped |

The recovery/error path at line 2630 calls `stop()` without a prior force-flush, silently dropping any buffered sub-minChars tail.

**Provenance**: `introduced by` fd15704c775 (Peter Steinberger, 2026-01-09) — original coalescer implementation. **Confidence**: clear.

## Regression Test Plan

6 new regression tests across 2 files cover:
- stop() delivers buffered text (regression for the exact reported bug)
- stop() respects abort state (safety guard)
- stop() after force-flush is idempotent (no double-delivery for the normal path)
- stop() preserves isCommentary (commentary suppression gates still apply)
- Pipeline-level stop() without prior force-flush delivers buffered text
- Pipeline-level stop() flushes multiple coalesced chunks

## User-visible / Behavior Changes 📌

Telegram DM users with `streaming.mode="block"`: long multi-paragraph replies now deliver the complete text including the final tail. Previously the last ~300–600 chars could be silently dropped.

## Security Impact (required) 📌

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x64)
- Runtime/container: Node 22.19
- Model/provider: N/A (coalescer-level fix, model-independent)
- Integration/channel: Telegram (block streaming mode)
- Relevant config (redacted): `channels.telegram.streaming.mode = "block"`

### Steps

1. Configure Telegram channel with `streaming.mode = "block"`
2. Trigger a long multi-paragraph DM reply (e.g., ask for a detailed explanation)
3. Observe the final text tail arrives complete (previously dropped)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required) 📌

- Verified scenarios: 6 new regression tests passing (coalescer + pipeline level), all 176 existing tests passing
- Edge cases checked: abort guard, idempotent after force-flush, minChars threshold, isCommentary preservation, multi-chunk coalescing

## Compatibility / Migration 📌

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict 📌

- **Best fix**: Yes. Fixing `stop()` at the coalescer level covers ALL callers (both the safe path at 1805 and the unsafe path at 2630) without requiring each call site to remember to force-flush first.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The coalescer is 252 lines and well-scoped; the fix reuses existing helpers (`copyReplyPayloadMetadata`, `resetBuffer`, `onFlush`) and follows existing fire-and-forget patterns (`void onFlush(...)`).
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Change line 2630 to add `await flush({force:true})` before `stop()` — rejected because it only fixes one call site; the coalescer invariant "stop may drop text" remains a footgun
  2. Expose `flushOnEnqueue` in `BlockStreamingCoalesceSchema` — tracked separately in #102580; not a fix for the existing loss path

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude (via open-source-pr skill) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analyzed issue #102578, traced root cause to `stop: () => clearIdleTimer()` at block-reply-coalescer.ts:224, implemented `deliverBufferedBeforeStop` to synchronously flush buffered text

## Risks and Mitigations 📌

**Highest Risk Area**: `stop()` is called from multiple paths (normal finalization, error recovery, agent cleanup). A synchronous `onFlush` call could theoretically trigger downstream errors that were previously silent.

**Mitigation Methods**: The flush is fire-and-forget (`void onFlush(...)`) — errors in the async delivery are handled by the transport layer, same as every other `void flush()` / `void onFlush()` call in the coalescer (6 existing call sites). The `shouldAbort()` guard prevents delivery during an active abort. The payload construction is the same shape used in `flush()` (lines 90-98).

**Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. The change only affects the case where `stop()` is called with buffered text — previously the text was silently dropped, now it's delivered. All other paths are unchanged.

---

Related to #102578

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independently incorrect things:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** had a single-char logic bug (`!==` for `===`) that forced explicit completions config to Responses.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** shared the same predicate, but after model resolution the `api` field carries no provenance bit — per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config and catalog default `api: "openai-completions"` are identical strings. Need to inspect raw config to distinguish them.

The fix:

1. **`hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig()`** — checks BOTH `config.models.providers.openai.api` (provider-level) AND `config.models.providers.openai.models[].api` (per-model) to distinguish user intent from catalog defaults.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport()`** — rewritten with own catalog-normalization logic, decoupled from `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel`** — checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before normalizing. Returns model unchanged when user explicitly configured completions.

4. **`normalizeTransport`** — same check. Returns `undefined` (no override) when user explicitly configured completions.

## User Impact

Users who configure `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider level or on a specific model row now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — real production import exercising `buildOpenAIProvider()`:**

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs
[PASS] resolved: catalog → Responses: want=openai-responses got=openai-responses
[PASS] resolved: provider-level explicit completions: want=openai-completions got=openai-completions
[PASS] resolved: per-model explicit completions: want=openai-completions got=openai-completions
[PASS] transport: catalog → Responses: want=openai-responses got=openai-responses
[PASS] transport: provider explicit → undefined: want=undefined got=undefined
[PASS] transport: per-model explicit → undefined: want=undefined got=undefined

6/6 passed
```

The proof script imports `buildOpenAIProvider()` from the actual production module and exercises both `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks against all three config levels (catalog-default, provider-level, per-model).

**Test regression:**

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs
→ exit 0
```

**Observed result after fix:** All six scenarios pass. Per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config is now correctly distinguished from catalog defaults and respected by both `normalizeResolvedModel` (preserves `"openai-completions"` api) and `normalizeTransport` (returns `undefined`, no Responses override).

**What was not tested:** Real OpenAI API endpoint E2E. The proof exercises the exact callback functions the gateway calls; API key validity is a separate concern.

## Regression Test Plan

- `$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 45 tests passed**
- `$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts --run` — **2 passed, 246 tests passed**
- `$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs` — **exit 0**
- `$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs` — **6/6 passed**

## Root Cause

In `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`, `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` had a single-character logic error (`!==` for `===`) that inverted the explicit-config guard. Additionally, `normalizeOpenAITransport` shared the same predicate but the resolved model's `api` field has no provenance — a per-model user config and the catalog default are indistinguishable strings. The only way to separate them is to inspect the raw config, which the `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` helper now does.

target.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue
target.body:
Fixes #79589

## Problem

Upstream added priority scheduling (foreground/normal/background) via insertion-sort at enqueue time (#82765). Within a static priority tier, older background work can still sit behind later background work indefinitely when the lane stays busy.

## Fix

Implement a **foreground-preserving one-tier aging** policy:

- After `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30s), an entry is promoted by **exactly one priority tier** (`priority + 1`).
- Background (-1) ages to normal (0), still below fresh foreground (1).
- Fresh user/foreground work always runs before aged background.
- Aged background still beats fresh background at the same static priority.

This intentionally does **not** promote aged work to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` or above fresh foreground. The contract is fairness among same-or-lower tiers without starving interactive work.

Files:
- `lanes.ts`: export `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS`
- `command-queue.ts`: `effectivePriority()` (+1 after threshold) and `pickNextIndex()` (effective priority, then oldest enqueue time, then sequence)
- `command-queue.test.ts`: one-tier aging regression tests using `enqueueCommandInLane(CommandLane.Main, ...)`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Command-lane drain selects aged background before fresh background after 30s, while still preferring fresh foreground over aged background (one-tier aging).

**Real environment tested:** macOS, Node from the local OpenClaw checkout, branch `feat/command-queue-priority` at head `41cd18a776`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /tmp/oc-75299
node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
```

**Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched branch:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
 ✓ command queue > preserves foreground priority over aged background work
 ✓ command queue > promotes aged background above fresh background (one-tier starvation guard)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 30 skipped (32)
```

Source confirmation of the one-tier policy:

```console
$ grep -n "STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS\|return entry.priority" src/process/lanes.ts src/process/command-queue.ts
src/process/lanes.ts:15:export const STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS = 30_000;
src/process/command-queue.ts:282:  if (Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt >= STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS) {
src/process/command-queue.ts:283:    return entry.priority + 1;
src/process/command-queue.ts:285:  return entry.priority;
```

Behavioral contract exercised by the two tests:
1. Aged background then fresh foreground drain order: `["foreground", "background"]`
2. Aged background then fresh background drain order: `["aged-bg", "fresh-bg"]`

**Observed result after fix:** One-tier aging raises background to normal after 30s so it beats later background work, while fresh foreground still wins over aged background. Policy, comments, tests, and this proof describe the same contract.

**What was not tested:** Live gateway under wall-clock multi-session contention with real cron/foreground traffic.

target.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization
target.body:
Fixes #90010
Fixes #79588

## Summary

Improve compaction identifier survival with transcript-wide extraction and quality-guard retry hints. Fixes two security/correctness issues found during review:

**Fix 1 — Sanitize string-encoded JSON arguments before extraction**: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` now parses string-encoded tool arguments as JSON and passes the parsed object through `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before identifier scanning. Previously, string arguments (e.g. OpenAI's JSON-stringified format) were appended raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`.

**Fix 2 — Fail strict compaction when cap recovery cannot fit**: When strict mode detects that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, compaction is now cancelled instead of returning a summary with known identifier loss. This prevents the session from continuing in a state where strict-required identifiers are silently dropped.

## Changed files

- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts` — Parse string args as JSON, sanitize via `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before appending; non-JSON strings still pass through
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` — Cancel compaction (return `{ cancel: true }` with reason) when strict cap recovery overflows instead of silently skipping
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` — Three regression tests: string-encoded JSON credential sanitization, non-JSON passthrough, strict-mode cap overflow cancel

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Two security/correctness issues in compaction identifier survival. (1) `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` appended string-encoded tool arguments raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`. (2) When strict mode detected that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, the summary was returned with known identifier loss instead of cancelling compaction.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5 arm64, Node v22.19.0, pnpm v11.2.2. Built from source on branch `compaction-identifier-survival-validation` at `/tmp/wt-75336`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Create proof script exercising production `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers`, `extractOpaqueIdentifiers`, `extractIdentifiersFromMessages`, `computeLostIdentifiers`, and `capCompactionSummary`:

```typescript
import {
  extractMessageTextForIdentifiers,
  extractOpaqueIdentifiers,
  extractIdentifiersFromMessages,
  computeLostIdentifiers,
} from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.js";
import { testing } from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.js";
const { capCompactionSummary, MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS } = testing;
```

Step 2. Validate Fix 1, string-encoded JSON args with credential `token` field:

```typescript
const msg = {
  role: "assistant",
  content: [{
    type: "functionCall", id: "call_1", name: "configure",
    arguments: '{"token":"deadbeef12345678","endpoint":"https://api.acme.io/v2"}',
  }],
};
const text = extractMessageTextForIdentifiers(msg);
assert(!text.includes("deadbeef12345678"));    // credential redacted
assert(text.includes("https://api.acme.io/v2")); // non-credential survives
```

Step 3. Validate Fix 2, capping loses identifiers and recovery overflows:

```typescript
const transcriptIds = extractIdentifiersFromMessages([
  { role: "user", content: "deploy hash a1b2c3d4e5f6" },
]);
const oversized = "## Decisions\nKeep flow.\n## Exact identifiers\n"
  + "x".repeat(MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS) + "\na1b2c3d4e5f6";
const capped = capCompactionSummary(oversized);
const lost = computeLostIdentifiers(transcriptIds, capped);
assert(lost.length > 0);  // identifier at tail truncated by capping
const recovered = `${capped}\n\n## Exact identifiers (recovered)\n- ${lost[0]}`;
assert(recovered.length > MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS); // recovery overflows
```

Step 4. Run `npx tsx proof-75336.ts` from the patched branch.

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ cd /tmp/wt-75336 && npx tsx proof-75336.ts

[Proof 1] String-encoded JSON args sanitization
  PASS credential token value is redacted from string args
  PASS non-credential endpoint survives sanitization
  PASS hex identifier extractor does not capture redacted credential
  PASS non-JSON string args pass through for extraction

[Proof 2] Identifier loss detection after capping
  PASS transcript identifiers extracted from messages
  PASS hex identifier normalized to uppercase
  PASS capped summary respects size limit
  PASS identifier at tail is lost after capping
  PASS recovery block exceeds cap (triggers cancel in strict mode)

Results: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Observed result after fix:

Fix 1: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` no longer leaks credential-field values from string-encoded JSON arguments. The `token` field value `deadbeef12345678` is redacted by `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before the hex identifier extractor can capture it. Non-credential fields and non-JSON strings pass through normally.

Fix 2: When strict mode detects identifier loss after capping and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000 chars), compaction is cancelled with a diagnostic reason instead of returning a summary with known missing identifiers. The cancel reason is stored via `setCompactionSafeguardCancelReason` for downstream diagnostics.

target.title: fix: relay Claude CLI assistant partial messages as streaming deltas
target.body:
Fixes #86050

## Summary

Relay Claude CLI assistant records as streaming deltas so the WebChat UI shows progressive output instead of waiting for the full response.

**Fix 1**: Parse `assistant` records from the Claude CLI JSONL stream and forward their text content as `chat.delta` events.

**Fix 2**: Gate on `stop_reason` using a positive partial signal: only forward records where `stop_reason` is explicitly present and `null` (the documented Claude CLI partial marker). Complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped to avoid duplicating the final message. Records without `stop_reason` at all are ignored as ambiguous (could be complete messages from custom `claude-stream-json` backends).

## Changed files

- `src/agents/cli-output.ts` -- Added `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` with positive `stop_reason: null` guard
- `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` -- Tests covering partial forwarding, complete-message skip, absent-stop_reason rejection, and edge cases

## Verification

All tests use the documented `stop_reason: null` marker for partial messages:
- `stop_reason: null` (explicit) -> text forwarded as streaming delta
- `stop_reason: "end_turn"` -> record skipped (complete message, not a partial)
- `stop_reason` absent -> record skipped (not a confirmed partial; prevents false delivery from custom backends)
- Non-assistant record types -> ignored by the parser
- Malformed content arrays -> returns null without throwing
- Mixed text + tool_use content -> text extracted, tool_use entries ignored

Fixes #86050

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Claude CLI assistant records are not relayed as streaming deltas, so WebChat waits for the full response. The `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function requires a positive partial signal (`stop_reason: null` explicitly present) to skip complete messages and forward only true streaming partials as `chat.delta` events.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from branch `fix/gateway-stream-relay` at `/tmp/proof-86649`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Build from branch and verify the partial assistant delta parser is active in compiled production code.
Step 2. Feed four Claude CLI JSONL records through the production `createCliJsonlStreamingParser`: two partials (`stop_reason: null`), one complete (`stop_reason: "end_turn"`), and one ambiguous (no `stop_reason` field).

Evidence after fix: terminal output from the patched build:

The partial assistant delta parser and its `stop_reason: null` guard are active in the compiled production bundle:

```console
$ grep -n "parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta\|stop_reason.*null\|partialDelta" dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js
216:function parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta(params) {
220:if (!isRecord$1(message) || !("stop_reason" in message) || message.stop_reason !== null) return null;
394:const partialDelta = parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta({
402:if (partialDelta) {
403:assistantText = partialDelta.text;
404:params.onAssistantDelta(partialDelta);
```

Runtime exercise of the production parser with Claude CLI JSONL event shapes:

```console
$ npx tsx proof-exercise.ts
=== Feeding Claude CLI JSONL records through production parser ===

Input record 1 (partial, stop_reason: null):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"}]

Input record 2 (partial, stop_reason: null, extended text):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]

Input record 3 (complete, stop_reason: "end_turn"):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer to your question."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Complete message skipped (no new delta), avoiding duplicate delivery

Input record 4 (no stop_reason field, ambiguous source):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Some response"}]},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Record without stop_reason skipped (not a confirmed partial)

=== Summary ===
Total records fed: 4
Partial deltas relayed: 2
Delta breakdown:
  [0] delta="Here is" (cumulative: "Here is")
  [1] delta=" the answer" (cumulative: "Here is the answer")

Before fix: Records 1-2 would not emit deltas (assistant type was ignored).
After fix: Records 1-2 relay as streaming deltas. Records 3-4 correctly skipped.
No duplicate final text delivered.
```

Observed result after fix: The compiled production code at `dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js:216-220` contains the `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function with the positive partial signal guard (`stop_reason !== null`). At line 394, the main parser calls this function as a fallback when no raw stream delta is available. Runtime exercise confirms: assistant records with `stop_reason: null` relay as incremental streaming deltas (`"Here is"` then `" the answer"`), complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped (preventing duplicate delivery), and ambiguous records without `stop_reason` are also skipped (preventing false delivery from custom backends).

What was not tested: Live Claude CLI session with real streaming output over the gateway WebSocket connection. The fix exercises the production parser against the documented Claude CLI JSONL protocol shapes. End-to-end WebChat/TUI display was not verified.

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: route assistant-record partials through commentary classification.

- When classification is active, partial assistant text buffers into `pendingClaudeText` like stream_event text
- Assistant partials that include `tool_use` flush pending narration to `onCommentaryText`

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-output.test.ts -t "partial"

```

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** File-source SecretRef in `messages.tts.personas.<id>.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey` is not resolved at runtime, causing `elevenlabs: not configured`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v22.19.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-89607`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/wt-89607
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm build

  # Verify the persona-level collector is in the production bundle
  cat dist/runtime-config-collectors-tts-BgBmCuWf.js

  # Run the regression tests
  npx vitest run src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  The persona-level iteration is active in the production bundle:

  ```console
  $ cat dist/runtime-config-collectors-tts-BgBmCuWf.js
  ...
  const personas = params.tts.personas;
  if (isRecord(personas)) for (const [personaId, persona] of Object.entries(personas)) {
  if (!isRecord(persona)) continue;
  const personaProviders = persona.providers;
  if (!isRecord(personaProviders)) continue;
  for (const [providerId, providerConfig] of Object.entries(personaProviders)) {
  if (!isRecord(providerConfig)) continue;
  collectProviderApiKeyAssignment({
  providerId,
  providerConfig,
  pathPrefix: `${params.pathPrefix}.personas.${personaId}`,
  ...
  ```

  Terminal confirms all 5 new tests exercise the persona SecretRef collection:

  ```console
  $ npx vitest run src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from top-level TTS providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from persona-level TTS provider overrides
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects SecretRefs from both top-level and persona-level providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > skips personas without providers
  ✓ collectTtsApiKeyAssignments > collects persona refs with agent-level path prefix
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  5 passed (5)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Production bundle at `dist/runtime-config-collectors-tts-BgBmCuWf.js` iterates persona-level providers and calls `collectProviderApiKeyAssignment` for each, ensuring file-source SecretRefs at `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` are resolved before reaching the TTS plugin.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway with an ElevenLabs account and file-source secret provider, triggering `openclaw infer tts convert` to confirm audio synthesis succeeds with the resolved key.

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: include global persona TTS refs in agent-runtime targets.

- Added `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` to `STATIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_BASE_TARGET_IDS`
- Extended the agent-runtime target coverage assertion to require both global and agent-level persona paths

Terminal confirmation on branch head:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cli/command-secret-targets.test.ts -t "persona TTS targets in the agent runtime"
 ✓ command secret target ids > includes persona TTS targets in the agent runtime command target set

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 39 skipped (40)
```

target.title: fix(text): keep five src-side text truncations UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `src/`-side text-truncation call sites still use raw `String.prototype.slice()` (or template-string slicing) with no UTF-16 surrogate-pair awareness. When an emoji or other supplementary Unicode character lands exactly on the cap, the slice can leave a dangling high surrogate that downstream provider / prompt / log consumers may treat as malformed text.

| File | Site | Cap | Visibility |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `src/cli/plugins-list-format.ts:19` | `plugin.description` truncation in CLI row | 57 chars | user-facing terminal output |
| `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts:75` | `formatHookErrorForLog` truncation | `MAX_HOOK_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (500) | log line per hook failure |
| `src/auto-reply/fallback-state.ts:33` | `truncateFallbackReasonPart` for fallback reason text | 80 chars (configurable) | fallback notice surfaced in chat |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.ts:117` | `generateConversationLabel` output cap | `maxLength` (default 128) | short session label surfaced in UI |

Each follows the same pattern that has already landed in 30+ merged UTF-16 PRs (e.g. #102087, #102466, #102496, #102085, #102332, #102090, #102266, #102246, #102378, #102464, #102467, #102470, #102483, #102484, #102477).

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw `slice()` / `.slice(0, N)` patterns with `truncateUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` (re-exported via `src/utils.js`). The helper preserves the existing cap for ordinary text and only backs up by one code unit when the cap would split a surrogate pair — matching the contract every other UTF-16 fix in this wave uses.

The helper is the canonical one (already imported by `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts`, `src/talk/fast-context-runtime.ts`, `src/agents/bash-process-references.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/bash-command.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts`, etc.), so no new helper surface is added.

**Scope note**: An earlier version of this PR also covered `src/auto-reply/reply/post-compaction-context.ts:120`, but that site was already covered by #102515 (lsr911, merged) which imports `truncateUtf16Safe` directly from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The current branch drops that site to avoid import churn around an already-covered file.

## User Impact

The four sites now keep their truncation caps but never produce a lone surrogate at the boundary. No behavior change for ASCII / CJK content; the only difference is at the exact boundary where the cap lands inside a surrogate pair.

No config, environment, default, SDK, protocol, or migration change. No public API change. No new dependency.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (after-fix, drives each changed truncation path with an emoji crossing the cap)

A standalone harness imports `truncateUtf16Safe` from `src/utils.ts` exactly as the four PR sites use it, drives each production call through the helper with emoji-density input crafted so the cap lands inside an astral code-point's surrogate pair, and verifies the output has no lone surrogate. The harness also runs the same input through raw `String.prototype.slice` to show what the bug used to look like.

```
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-102630.mjs

site 1 (plugins-list-format, cap 57) -> 57 chars, lone surrogate: false
  output: "🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 🎨 "
site 2 (fire-and-forget, cap 500) -> 500 chars, lone surrogate: false
site 3 (fallback-state, cap 79) -> 79 chars, lone surrogate: false
site 4 (conversation-label-generator, cap 128) -> 128 chars, lone surrogate: false

=== Raw slice comparison (showing what the bug used to look like) ===
plugins-list-format, cap 57: raw slice lone surrogate = true, helper lone surrogate = false
fire-and-forget, cap 500: raw slice lone surrogate = false, helper lone surrogate = false
fallback-state, cap 79: raw slice lone surrogate = true, helper lone surrogate = false
conversation-label-generator, cap 128: raw slice lone surrogate = false, helper lone surrogate = false

=== PASS: four production sites keep output surrogate-safe at the cap ===
```

Two of the four sites (cap 57 and cap 79) show the bug clearly: a raw `slice()` would split the emoji and leave a dangling surrogate, while `truncateUtf16Safe` backs off by one code unit. The other two sites happen to land just inside an emoji boundary on the chosen input; the helper still produces the expected length with no surrogate.

The proof uses no private paths, tokens, or user data — only the public `truncateUtf16Safe` helper and synthetic emoji-dense inputs. Reproduction command is in the harness file; the harness exits with a non-zero status on any unexpected length or surrogate.

### Behavior proof

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `${plugin.description.slice(0, 57)}...` | `${truncateUtf16Safe(plugin.description, 57)}...` |
| `(formatted \|\| "unknown error").slice(0, MAX_HOOK_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH)` | `truncateUtf16Safe(formatted \|\| "unknown error", MAX_HOOK_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH)` |
| `${text.slice(0, Math.max(0, max - 1)).trimEnd()}…` | `${truncateUtf16Safe(text, Math.max(0, max - 1)).trimEnd()}…` |
| `text.slice(0, maxLength)` | `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxLength)` |

All four sites preserve their existing length-based `if (text.length <= max) return text;` short-circuit; the helper only operates on the truncate branch.

| `auto-reply/fallback-state.ts:33` (fallback reason) | `FALLBACK_REASON_PART_MAX` (80) | same | same | `src/auto-reply/fallback-state.test.ts` |
| `auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.ts:117` (label) | `maxLength` (default 128) | same | same | `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts` |

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip scheduled heartbeat on idle sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled heartbeats fire every ~30 minutes regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks, silently burning API tokens with no user to receive output. A single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit (#98556).

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults session staleness — `lastInteractionAt` has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception but was never read by the heartbeat runner.
- **Solution**: Gate only ordinary scheduled interval heartbeats (`intent: "scheduled"`) on the resolved session's last interaction time. If `lastInteractionAt` or `sessionStartedAt` is older than 7 days, skip with `reason: "session-idle"`.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (+18 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (+208 lines, 8 test cases)
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, no public API changes. Event/manual/immediate wake intents are not gated. Existing behavior for active sessions is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls firing every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This fix provides a runtime safety guard using a positive-match pattern (`intent: "scheduled"`) to avoid the event-wake delivery regression that blocked the previous attempt (#100852).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Scheduled heartbeats skip on sessions idle longer than 7 days; all other wake intents (event/immediate/manual) are unaffected.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)

$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)

$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Real runtime proof** — direct `runHeartbeatOnce()` call with real session store, real workspace, and real HEARTBEAT.md:

```console
$ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts
=== Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

    status: skipped, reason: empty-heartbeat-file
  ✅ Active session (1 min idle) + scheduled
    status: skipped, reason: session-idle
  ✅ Idle session (8 days) + scheduled → skip
    status: skipped, reason: empty-heartbeat-file
  ✅ Idle session (8 days) + event → NOT skipped

=== Results: 3 passed, 0 failed ===
```

| Test | Scenario | Intent | lastInteractionAt | Idle gate fired? |
|------|----------|--------|-------------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Active session | `scheduled` | 1 min ago | No (different skip: empty-heartbeat-file) |
| 2 | Idle 8 days | `scheduled` | 8 days ago | ✅ Yes → `session-idle` |
| 3 | Idle 8 days | `event` | 8 days ago | ✅ No → event not gated |

**Matrix: idle gate behavior by wake intent**

| Intent | Session state | lastInteractionAt | Result |
|--------|--------------|-------------------|--------|
| `scheduled` | Active (1 min idle) | now - 1m | `ran` (no gate) |
| `scheduled` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `skipped / session-idle` |
| `scheduled` | No entry | undefined | `ran` (no gate) |
| `scheduled` | Exactly at boundary | now - 7d | `ran` (> threshold, not >=) |
| `event` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |
| `immediate` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |
| `manual` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |

**Fallback chain**:

| Available fields | Behavior |
|-----------------|----------|
| `lastInteractionAt` exists + >7d | Skip |
| `lastInteractionAt` missing, `sessionStartedAt` exists + >7d | Skip (fallback) |
| Neither `lastInteractionAt` nor `sessionStartedAt` | Allow (cannot determine staleness) |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Scheduled heartbeats on sessions idle >7 days: skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. Event/manual/immediate heartbeats on idle sessions: unaffected.
  3. Sessions with recent interaction: unaffected (no behavioral change).
  4. Sessions with no entry or insufficient timestamps: unaffected.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts`) performs 13 skip checks but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

## Regression Test Plan

8 new unit tests cover the idle gate (active session, stale session, all 4 wake intents, fallback to sessionStartedAt, no-entry, boundary). 43 existing heartbeat tests confirm zero regression.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see scheduled heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: Active session, idle session (8 days), all 4 wake intents, no session entry, exactly at 7-day boundary.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined (falls back to `sessionStartedAt`), both undefined, no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for idle sessions; heartbeat behavior for active sessions is completely unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Positive-match on `intent === "scheduled"` avoids the deny-list regression that blocked #100852. The injection point in `runHeartbeatOnce()` (after all other skip conditions, before preflight) is the right boundary because the session entry is already resolved and all four wake intents are known.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because it requires a configured `SessionResetPolicy` which may not be present.
  2. Using `session.resetPolicy.idleMinutes` if configured — over-engineered for a safety guard.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout. That feature requires a product decision and is tracked separately. This PR provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard (7-day threshold) that prevents runaway cost while #14051 is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate low-frequency heartbeat tasks (e.g., a weekly report).
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold uses strict greater-than (`>`, not `>=`), so a weekly heartbeat that fires on day 7 still runs. Only sessions idle longer than 7 days are affected.
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days.
**Scope limitation**: Auth error backoff (repeated `authentication_error` after spend cap) is not addressed — it is a separate defense-in-depth concern tracked in #98556.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

---

Related to #98556

target.title: fix: bind bun x exec approvals to the inner command like bunx
target.body:
Related: #102035

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an inconsistency where exec approvals for `bun x <pkg>` bind to the
outer wrapper string while the equivalent `bunx <pkg>` binds to the inner
command. PR #102035 bound durable package-manager exec approvals to the inner
trust target for npm / npx / pnpm / yarn / bunx, but
`resolveKnownPackageManagerExecInvocation` has no `bun` case, so `bun x <pkg>`
falls through to `not-package-manager`.

Concretely, on current main:

- `bunx tsx ./run.ts` unwraps: allow-always persists against the inner `tsx`
  and later invocations match on `tsx`.
- The equivalent `bun x tsx ./run.ts` does not unwrap: allow-always cannot
  persist at all (`bun` is an interpreter-like executable, so the decision
  falls to one-shot), and a pre-existing outer `bun` allowlist entry matches
  the whole invocation without inner binding.

This is a consistency gap, not an approval bypass: the un-unwrapped form still
requires approval (the whole outer string is the trust target).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `case "bun"` that unwraps only when the dispatched subcommand is
unambiguous. Two models exist for how a space-valued bun global (for example
`--cwd ./pkg`) interacts with subcommand selection: bun's root selector has
been observed to skip dash tokens without consuming their values, while this
repo's shipped script-operand hardening (`src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts`)
models bun as consuming a separate value for the known globals. The resolver
computes the selected command under both models and unwraps only when both
select the same `x` token — plain flags (`--silent`, `--bun`) and inline
values (`--cwd=./pkg`) qualify; the tail then unwraps through the shared bunx
parser (`unwrapDirectPackageExecInvocation`), with an explicit `--` separator
handled the way the npm `x` alias handles it, so `bun x` and `bunx` bind the
same inner trust targets for the forms both accept. Every form whose dispatch
depends on the model fails closed as `unsafe-exec` — a space-valued global
whose value is literally `x` (`bun -c x sh ...`), a space-valued global ahead
of `x` (`bun --cwd ./pkg x ...`), unknown globals ahead of a possible `x`,
bare `bun x`, shell-call tails (`-c` / `--call`), and `--` ahead of the
selector — so neither a wrong inner binding nor a stale outer-`bun` fallback
match is possible for those forms. The known-globals table is the shipped
node-host one, now exported from this module and imported by
invoke-system-run-plan so there is a single source.

This change is limited to `bun x`. Other bun invocations — `bun run
<script>`, `bun <file>`, and `bun exec` (a shell-string carrier rather than a
package runner) — keep their previous classification: for the affected
approval consumers they continue to fall back to ordinary outer-command
handling.

## User Impact

Approving `bun x <pkg>` with allow-always now persists and matches against the
inner command, the same as `bunx <pkg>`, npm, pnpm, and yarn exec forms.
Matching the treatment the other wrappers already received, a durable
allowlist entry for the outer `bun` binary no longer matches `bun x ...`
invocations whole; the inner command is the trust target.

## Evidence

Boundary capture driving the real resolver, authorization plan, and allowlist
matching (`node --import tsx`, real executables on a temp `PATH`, no mocks).

Before (base `9614129c2b`):

```
["bunx","tsx","./run.ts"] -> {"kind":"unwrapped","argv":["tsx","./run.ts"]}
["bun","x","tsx","./run.ts"] -> {"kind":"not-package-manager"}
["bun","-c","x","sh","-c","id > marker"] -> {"kind":"not-package-manager"}
["bun","--cwd","./pkg","x","tsx","./run.ts"] -> {"kind":"not-package-manager"}
"bunx tsx ./run.ts" -> allow-always persists {"pattern":".../tsx"}
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" -> {"kind":"one-shot","reasons":["no-reusable-pattern"]}
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" + inner tsx entry -> allowlistSatisfied=false
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" + outer bun entry -> allowlistSatisfied=true
"bun -c x sh -c 'id > marker'" + outer bun entry -> allowlistSatisfied=true
```

After (this PR):

```
["bun","x","tsx","./run.ts"] -> {"kind":"unwrapped","argv":["tsx","./run.ts"]}
["bun","run","build"] -> {"kind":"not-exec"}
["bun","-c","x","sh","-c","id > marker"] -> {"kind":"unsafe-exec"}
["bun","--cwd","./pkg","x","tsx","./run.ts"] -> {"kind":"unsafe-exec"}
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" -> allow-always persists {"pattern":".../tsx"}
"bun x sh -c 'id > marker'" -> {"kind":"one-shot","reasons":["no-reusable-pattern"]}
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" + inner tsx entry -> allowlistSatisfied=true
"bun x tsx ./run.ts" + outer bun entry -> allowlistSatisfied=false
"bun -c x sh -c 'id > marker'" + outer bun entry -> allowlistSatisfied=false
"bun --cwd ./pkg x tsx ./run.ts" + inner tsx entry -> allowlistSatisfied=false
```

Tests (all green locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, 139 tests across
the touched shards):

- `src/infra/package-manager-exec-wrapper.test.ts` (new): bunx-parity unwrap,
  flag and inline-value and double-dash tails, non-exec forms (`bun run` /
  `bun ./x.ts` / `bun install` / `bun exec`), and model-dependent forms
  failing closed: each space-valued global (`-c` / `--config` / `--cwd` /
  `--env-file`) with `x` in value position and with `x` after a value token,
  unknown globals ahead of `x`, bare `bun x`, `--call` tails, and `--`.
- `src/infra/exec-allow-always-persistence.test.ts`: persists `bun x` approvals
  against the inner executable; keeps `bun x` shell carriers and
  space-valued-global forms one-shot (no durable pattern in either direction).
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts`: rejects stale outer `bun`
  entries for `bun x` carriers and space-valued-global forms; matches
  inner-executable entries for `bun x` while refusing inner matching for
  `bun --cwd ./pkg x ...`, alongside the existing package-manager parity
  cases.
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts`: `bun x tsx file` mutable
  operand fixture next to the existing `bunx tsx file` case.

`oxfmt --check` and the typecheck lanes pass on the touched files locally;
the remaining lint and check lanes run in CI.

target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR2/5 in the durable runtime stack. It implements the durable runtime core on top of canonical PR1 #101828, adding persistent runtime state, recovery/orchestration primitives, gateway/operator surfaces, and tests while preserving the PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR2/5
- Canonical upstream gate: PR1 #101828 is 🦐 gold shrimp / threshold-met.
- PR: #102495
- Branch: `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-core-v2-pr101828-ready`
- Current head: `e37c3d5840` (`fix(chat): restore pairing QR display block`)
- Intended base: `origin/pr/101828` at `98ffd6a2fb`
- Next dependent PR: PR3 remains gated until PR2 reaches the `gold_shrimp_schrimp` threshold.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent/session work currently has runtime state and lifecycle edges that are difficult to recover, replay, or reason about across process failures. This PR adds the durable runtime core needed to persist task/run state, recover or fan in work safely, expose gateway controls, and keep embedded-agent session effects typed and observable while preserving canonical PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Scope

- Durable runtime model, SQLite store, recovery/fan-in/orchestration primitives, worker surface, and gateway methods.
- Agent/session runtime effects and context refs needed for durable runs.
- Guardrails/tests for schema lifecycle, task completion policy, gateway protocol, and embedded-agent retry behavior.
- Webchat pairing QR display preservation so sensitive QR setup data is displayed transiently without being persisted into transcript history.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Does not submit PR3 durable agent restart/upgrade proof.
- Does not submit PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery-only stack item.
- Does not submit PR5 opt-in workflow worker loop as a separately promoted stack item.
- Does not decide durable runtime product direction beyond implementing the accepted PR1 boundary.

## Base / diff reconciliation

- PR2 is maintained as a non-cumulative replay on canonical PR1 #101828, not as a cumulative stack against `main`.
- Reconciled against `origin/pr/101828` (`98ffd6a2fb`) and retained exactly the PR2 durable-runtime commits plus the QR repair commit.
- Replay conflict in `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts` was resolved by preserving `activeRunAbort.cleanup({ force: true })` while adding durable lifecycle close on undispatched failures.
- `git log --oneline --reverse origin/pr/101828..HEAD` now shows the PR2 replay plus repair:
  - `c851808aa3 feat(durable): add runtime foundation`
  - `c31b49c366 feat(durable): wire agent session runtime`
  - `1bb1edf8cc fix(durable): harden runtime store and controls`
  - `12a58c5ceb fix(durable): align runtime schema guardrails`
  - `099ffa5dbc fix(durable): type session effects on embedded runs`
  - `e37c3d5840 fix(chat): restore pairing QR display block`
- The QR repair restores mainline pairing QR sensitive-display behavior in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`: pairing QR channel-data detection, terminal/PNG QR display block rendering, sensitive-media handling, and final/broadcast display inclusion.

## Reviewer / ClawSweeper requirements addressed

- Authored `What Problem This Solves`: included above.
- Authored proof/evidence sections: included below.
- Stored data model / migration impact: named below; this PR adds durable SQLite runtime state/tables and serialized metadata.
- ClawSweeper actionable `krab` finding: fixed by restoring the transient `openclaw_pairing_qr` assistant display block while continuing to avoid transcript persistence of QR setup code.
- Dirty/conflicting base concern: reconciled to canonical PR1 #101828 for non-cumulative review and pushed as the PR head.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|

target.title: fix(agents): transcode unsupported image media_type before Anthropic replay
target.body:
Closes #102323

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on a Claude/Anthropic model with no media-understanding provider (so inbound images are forwarded as image blocks, not transcribed) would get **no reply at all** when they sent an iPhone HEIC photo — or any `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, or `image/bmp` image — that was already within OpenClaw's size and dimension limits.

The whole turn failed with an Anthropic `400 invalid_request_error` because the image's real `media_type` was forwarded verbatim, and Anthropic only accepts `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, or `image/webp`. The exact same image works on OpenAI and Gemini, so the failure was Anthropic-specific and looked like a silent message-loss bug to the user.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared image sanitizer (`src/agents/tool-images.ts`) is the single choke point that **every** image-bearing Anthropic path flows through before the provider adapter — current-turn prompt images, replayed session history, and tool-result images. The Anthropic adapters (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` and `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) only *build* blocks and forward `media_type` verbatim (`packages/ai` has no image backend, so it cannot transcode).

Previously the sanitizer only re-encoded when an image exceeded size/dimension limits; a within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP took an early return with its original `mimeType` intact. The fix makes the sanitizer transcode any image whose declared mime is outside the supported inline set to a supported type up front (via the existing `convertImageToPng`, which includes the BMP fallback), then runs the normal size/dimension ladder.

Note: relabeling `media_type` to `image/jpeg` without touching the bytes — as the issue's minimal suggestion implies — would still 400 on decode, so this transcodes the actual bytes. This also resolves the secondary symptom where `image/bmp` silently degraded to a text placeholder.

## User Impact

Users on Anthropic models with image passthrough can now send HEIC/HEIF/TIFF/BMP images (e.g. default iPhone photos) and get a normal reply, matching OpenAI and Gemini behavior. No config change or migration required.

## Evidence

### Full runtime proof — 18 tests across 3 files (`main` @ 03aca2c)

All three test files — the existing sanitizer tests, the backend-unavailable regression, and the end-to-end Anthropic transport capture — pass cleanly:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/tool-images.test.ts \
    src/agents/tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts \
    src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

|unit-fast| tool-images.test.ts
 ✓ shrinks oversized images to the configured byte limit
 ✓ sanitizes image arrays and reports drops
 ✓ shrinks images that exceed max dimension even if size is small
 ✓ corrects mismatched jpeg mimeType
 ✓ uses default image limits for non-finite options
 ✓ preserves data and mimeType on no-resize path
 ✓ preserves data and mimeType on resize path
 ✓ converts image blocks with missing data/mimeType to text
 ✓ screenshot-shaped tool result round-trips with valid image block
 ✓ screenshot-shaped tool result with malformed image produces text fallback
 ✓ drops malformed image base64 payloads
 ✓ transcodes an unsupported within-limit media_type to a supported type
 ✓ keeps a supported within-limit media_type byte-identical
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  13 passed (13)

|agents| anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts
 ✓ sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image

|agents| tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts
 ✓ keeps small header-verified images without probing the backend
 ✓ drops images that need resizing when the backend is unavailable
 ✓ drops unsupported-MIME images when the backend is unavailable   ← NEW
 ✓ does not pass through compressed images over the pixel cap
 Test Files  2 passed (2) | Tests  5 passed (5)

Total: 3 files passed, 18 tests passed, 0 failed
```

### Sanitizer unit + backend-unavailable coverage (`src/agents/tool-images.test.ts` + `src/agents/tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts`)

- **`transcodes an unsupported within-limit media_type to a supported type`** — feeds decodable, within-limit WebP bytes labeled `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, `image/bmp` and asserts the output mime is a supported inline type (jpeg/png/gif/webp) and no longer the original.
- **`keeps a supported within-limit media_type byte-identical`** — guards the fast path: `image/webp` bytes and mime pass through unmodified.
- **`drops unsupported-MIME images when the backend is unavailable`** (NEW) — when `convertImageToPng` throws `backendUnavailableError` for an `image/heic` input, the sanitizer returns a text fallback instead of crashing. The explicit `vi.doMock` factory exports `convertImageToPng` (was previously missing — ClawSweeper P2 blocker resolved).

### E2E Anthropic transport media_type capture (`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts`)

Drives the **real shared sanitizer** (`sanitizeImageBlocks`) into the **real Anthropic Messages transport** (`createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn`) and inspects the captured outgoing request body — the same "capture the outgoing `media_type`" method the issue used, but exercising the production code path end-to-end.

**Before fix (guard reverse-applied out of the worktree, test kept):**
```
 × sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image
AssertionError: expected 'image/heic' not to be 'image/heic' // Object.is equality
   expect(mediaTypes[0]).not.toBe("image/heic");
 Tests  1 failed (1)
```
The outgoing request body carried `media_type: "image/heic"` verbatim — the exact 400 trigger.

**After fix:**
```
 ✓ sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image
 Tests  1 passed (1)
```
The outgoing `media_type` is now a supported inline type (jpeg/png/gif/webp) and no longer `image/heic`.

### Edges covered

| Path | Test | Outcome |
|------|------|---------|
| Within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP → transcode to PNG | `tool-images.test.ts` | supported mime, bytes changed |
| Within-limit supported type (webp) → identity | `tool-images.test.ts` | same mime, same bytes |
| Backend unavailable → unsupported MIME drops as text | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | text fallback, no crash |
| Backend unavailable → small supported PNG passes through | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | image kept unchanged |
| Backend unavailable → oversized image drops as text | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | text fallback |
| Sanitizer → real Anthropic transport → captured body | `anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts` | media_type is supported |

### Fix-boundary verification

A trace confirmed all four Anthropic image paths (current-turn user image, replayed history, and tool results across both the packaged provider and the custom transport) route through `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` / `sanitizeSessionMessagesImages` / `sanitizeToolResultImages`, which all funnel into `resizeImageBase64IfNeeded`. No SDK/plugin/gateway path reaches the Anthropic adapters with image blocks unsanitized.

### Typecheck

`pnpm tsgo` clean for all changed files.

_All evidence above uses synthetic image fixtures generated in-test; no secrets, IPs, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints are included (the loopback transport uses a mocked fetch and a dummy `sk-ant-api03-test` placeholder key)._
